title: Litter picking on external grounds and entrances
audience: Cleaning operative working on external areas such as entrances, car parks, paths and grounds, under the site's approved procedure.
learningOutcomes: Barrier and sign an outdoor work area so that vehicles, colleagues and the public can see where work is happening.
Pick up litter, cigarette ends, gum and waste from the listed external surfaces and planting areas without disturbing the planting more than necessary.
Separate general litter from sharps and contaminated waste, and handle each category in the way the procedure requires.
Describe the post-job checks for equipment, personal hygiene and the external areas.

instruction.heading: Why litter picking carries more risk than it looks
instruction.body: Litter picking appears to be low-skill work, but the outdoor setting adds hazards that indoor cleaning does not have. Vehicles and pedestrians share the space. Hedges, verges and planting beds can hide sharps, broken glass and contaminated waste. Dust, pollen and bacteria can reach the skin and eyes. The aim of this lesson is to keep the worker visible and protected, to keep sharps and contaminated waste separate from general litter, and to leave the grounds clean and tidy without creating new hazards for other people.

instruction.heading: Equipment and personal protection
instruction.body: Check each litter picker and each sack before use, and wash the equipment as the procedure requires so that residues do not carry from one site to another. Wear the gloves issued to you at all times while picking. High-visibility clothing must be worn whenever you are picking litter, because you will be working outdoors where vehicles are moving. Always use the sharps containers and collection points the site has approved. Wash your hands thoroughly after each litter pick, even when the gloves seemed intact.

instruction.heading: Setting up the work area
instruction.body: Barrier off the area so that vehicles, employees and customers can clearly see where you are working. The boundary of the external area to be cleaned must be confirmed with the site before work starts. Do not start in an area that is not on the agreed boundary plan.

instruction.heading: Picking up litter and waste
instruction.body: Work through the external areas on the scope list: entrances, car parks, paving, paths, steps, ramps, walkways, terraces, ledges, signage, fixed seating, lighting columns, bollards and the outside of the premises. Pick up litter, cigarette ends, chewing gum and general dirt. Place general litter into the designated sacks. Keep your body out of hedgerows, and reach in with the litter picker where possible. Only a foot should go into a hedge bed, and only when the procedure allows it. Take sacks to the skip or the customer's designated collection area. Empty and replace all waste bins in their original positions.

instruction.heading: Sharps and contaminated waste
instruction.body: If you find a needle, syringe or other sharp, stop and mark the location clearly so no one else touches it. Call a trained colleague to bring the sharps container and dispose of the item under the sharps procedure for bodily fluids and sharps. Never pick up a sharp with your hands. Place all sharps in a rigid sharps container, never in a sack. Store the sharps containers in a locked storage area and dispose of them through the site's approved route. Litter pickers and bins must be washed regularly, and the needle-stick containers must be kept sealed.

instruction.heading: Protected areas and finishing the job
instruction.body: Some areas are protected by security screening, netting or protective cages. You may remove the protection temporarily to clear debris, dirt, dust and litter, but it must be replaced to its original condition before you leave. The finished area should look clean and tidy, be free of litter, gum, cigarette ends, staining and bodily fluid, and show no sign of food pests or vermin. Disinfectant may be used where it is appropriate. Remove barriers only after the area is clear and safe.

procedure: Confirm the external boundary of the work area with the site contact before starting.
Put on high-visibility clothing and gloves, then set up barriers and signs.
Check the litter pickers and sacks, and confirm the sharps container is at hand.
Work through the external surfaces and planting areas on the scope list, one section at a time.
Place general litter into designated sacks and keep your body out of hedgerows.
If a sharp or contaminated item is found, mark it, leave it in place, and call a trained colleague.
Place sharps only in a rigid container and never in a sack.
Empty bins and replace them in their original positions.
Take sacks to the skip or customer collection point.
Replace any protective screening, netting or cage removed during the work.
Wash the litter pickers and bins, wash your hands, and record the job.

workedExamples.situation: A worker litter picking a hedge bed beside a car park sees a syringe lying under a leaf pile.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What does the worker do next?
workedExamples.reasoning: The worker stops, does not touch the syringe, and marks the spot so no one else approaches it. A trained colleague brings the sharps container and removes the item under the sharps procedure. The worker keeps the rest of the bed out of reach until the item is removed, then finishes the bed and washes their hands.

workedExamples.situation: The entrance path is partly blocked by a delivery van while the worker is picking litter near the kerb.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How is the work area managed?
workedExamples.reasoning: The worker keeps the barrier and signs in place, moves the work to a safe section away from the van, and stays visible in high-visibility clothing. The worker does not step into the road to pick up litter, and reports to the site contact if the traffic risk cannot be controlled.

equipmentAndPpe: Litter pickers, washed and checked before use
Rigid sharps container, kept in a locked storage area
Approved disinfectant where the procedure allows it

commonErrors.error: Picking up a sharp with the hands or the litter picker and placing it in a sack.
commonErrors.prevention: Mark the sharp, leave it in place, and call a trained colleague to remove it into a rigid sharps container.

commonErrors.error: Working on the roadside without barriers or high-visibility clothing.
commonErrors.prevention: Set up barriers and signs first, and wear high-visibility clothing for the whole task.

commonErrors.error: Leaving protective screening or netting removed after the job.
commonErrors.prevention: Note each protection removed and replace it to its original condition before leaving.

commonErrors.error: Reaching deep into a hedge bed and disturbing planting or hidden hazards.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the body out of the hedge, use the litter picker, and move the work to a safer section if access is poor.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Sharps and contaminated waste must be handled by a trained person. Whether this lesson is enough for the sharps task depends on the site rule and the training the worker has had.
Work near vehicles must be barriered and marked, and high-visibility clothing worn.
Chemicals used for disinfection must be used as their label directs, with the safety data sheet available on site.
Stop work and call the site contact if the boundary is unclear, a sharp is found in a place you cannot reach safely, or a vehicle or member of the public enters the work area.

qualityStandard: All listed external surfaces are free of litter, cigarette ends, chewing gum, dirt, bodily fluid and staining.
Sharps and contaminated waste are in rigid containers only, and the containers are locked away.
Bins are emptied and returned to their original positions.
Protective screening, netting or cages are replaced to their original condition.
Barriers and signs are removed only after the area is clear and safe.
documentationEvidence: Job sheet with the boundary confirmed and the areas covered
Record of any sharp or contaminated item found, its location and the trained colleague who removed it
Record of any protective screening or netting moved and replaced
Disinfectant product and label reference used, if any
Any incident or near miss reported to the supervisor
summary: Barrier and sign the area, and wear high-visibility clothing for the whole task.
Never pick up a sharp by hand. Mark it, leave it, and call a trained colleague.
Keep sharps in rigid containers and general litter in sacks, and keep them separate.
Replace protective screening, empty bins to their positions, and wash equipment and hands after the job.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a worker wear when litter picking beside roads and vehicles?
options: Shorts and a sun hat, which are enough outdoors in warm weather
High-visibility clothing, gloves and any other PPE the site requires
A hard hat only, with no other protective clothing needed here
Nothing extra, because litter picking is light work on most sites

knowledgeChecks.question: A needle is found in a hedge bed. What is the correct first action?
options: Pick it up with a gloved hand and place it in general waste and move on to the next patch
Mark its location, keep others away from it, and call a trained colleague with a sharps container
Leave it, because the council will remove it later and walk on past it without a second look
Cover it with leaves and mark the spot and tell the site office about it later on

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should sharps collected during a litter pick be placed?
options: In an open bucket of water

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say about gloves while litter picking?
options: Pick with bare hands to feel for sharps
Wear the gloves issued to you at all times while picking
